additions.note: 3T-class multimodal reasoning model with 1M context, post-trained from Kimi K3 for coding, 3D creation, research, and agents. Available in Kimi apps, Work, Code, and the API as kimi-k3.1-pro. Full weights are promised by November 4, 2026, and are not yet public. Uses the October 23 official launch announcement; the research index is dated October 24.

Faster hosted K3.1 Pro variant released alongside the standard model, available as kimi-k3.1-pro-highspeed in the API and across Kimi products. Moonshot reports 2-3 times the speed; this is a publisher claim. Full model weights are promised by November 4, 2026, rather than available at launch.

Open small language model built on Gemma 4 E4B for local conversational agents, multi-turn tool use, and configurable reasoning with 64K context. Released checkpoint targets an approximately 4GB footprint on supported NVIDIA hardware. Distinct from October 15's Bolt 74B-A9B-24GB; the previously scheduled E4B release is now available.

Apache-2.0 interactive video world-generation model with public weights and code. Extends video segment by segment using text instructions, camera control, and a persistent KV cache. Includes distilled and quantized inference configurations. Uses the official repository's October 23 initial release, not its October 24 metadata update.

Canva Research's first image-generation foundation model, available in Dream Lab and through a public API. Separates composition planning from image rendering, with output up to 2K and support for editable design workflows. Faster Craft-fast and Craft-ultrafast variants are announced as upcoming, not released here.

Open satellite-embedding foundation model released with weights, training data, code, global annual embeddings, and a browser explorer. Produces 128-dimensional representations of 10-meter land pixels, with a reusable 64-dimensional subset. Governed by the OlmoEarth Artifact License; geospatial evaluation claims are separate from language-model rankings.

Apache-2.0 coding and agent model with 39.8B total parameters, approximately 2.5B active, and 262,144-token context. Public BF16 weights and SGLang serving kit support reasoning and multi-turn tool use. Uses the official checkpoint's October 21 initial release; benchmark results are publisher evaluations.

27B and 9B open decision models from Baseten's research lab, returning probabilities for choices, yes/no questions, and scores instead of free-form text. Released weights and hosted Baseten Model APIs support routing, classification, and verification. Leaderboard positions in the announcement are dated publisher claims.

On-device text-to-speech weights in 31M and 40M sizes, including language-specific and multilingual variants. English 31m is Apache-2.0; 40m variants use CC BY-NC terms. Uses the October 20 open-weight announcement, preceding the October 21 press release; distinct from April's private-beta announcement.
